test.title: Section 2 · social media and the hiring panel

texts.label: A
texts.title: Posting about work on social media: staff guidance

paragraphs.text: Posting about work on social media: staff guidance. The company recognises that many employees use social media in their private lives, and it has no wish to control what staff say about matters unconnected with their work. This guidance applies whenever you post something that mentions the company, its customers or your colleagues, or that could be linked to your job, including posts on personal accounts. It does not replace the rules on confidential information in the staff handbook, which still apply in full.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: You are welcome to share news that the company has already made public, such as job advertisements, product launches or charity events, and when you do so it is sensible to make clear that you work here. However, only the communications team may speak on behalf of the company. Staff must not reply to customer complaints that appear online, however unfair they seem; instead, send a link to the post to the communications team, who aim to respond within one working day.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Photographs taken at work need particular care. Before posting a picture that shows colleagues, ask their permission, and never post images that show computer screens, whiteboards or documents, as these may contain information that is not public. Photographs taken at the warehouse or in the production areas must not be posted at all, because of the risk of showing equipment or processes that competitors could copy.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: If you are unsure whether a post is acceptable, the simplest test is to ask whether you would be comfortable if both your manager and a customer read it. Posts that break this guidance may be treated as a disciplinary matter. Anyone who sees something online that worries them, such as a colleague being criticised or false information about the company, should report it to their manager rather than responding to it themselves.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Sitting on an interview panel. Most vacancies in the company are filled after an interview with a panel of three people: the manager of the team with the vacancy, a colleague from another department and a member of the human resources team, who chairs the panel. Before sitting on a panel for the first time, staff must complete the online course on fair recruitment, which takes about ninety minutes and must be repeated every three years.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Panel members receive the application forms at least two working days before the interviews. Candidates’ names, ages and addresses are removed from the forms before they are sent out, so that decisions about who to interview are based only on skills and experience. Each member scores the applications separately against the requirements in the job description, and the panel then meets to agree a shortlist; where members disagree strongly, the chair has the final say.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Every candidate is asked the same main questions in the same order, although panel members may ask follow-up questions to explore an answer in more detail. Questions about family plans, health or religion must never be asked. Members take notes during the interview and give each answer a score from one to five immediately afterwards, before discussing the candidate with the others, so that their first judgement is not influenced by anyone else.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: All notes and score sheets must be handed to the chair at the end of the day. They are kept by human resources for six months, as candidates are entitled to ask for feedback and, in some cases, to see the notes made about them. Panel members must not tell candidates the outcome themselves, even informally; the chair telephones the successful candidate, usually within three working days, and the others are informed by e-mail. Anyone who knows a candidate personally should tell the chair before the interviews and may be replaced on the panel.
paragraphs.label: D

document.title: Section 2 · social media and the hiring panel

topic.en: Two workplace texts: what staff may post about work on social media, and how an interview panel works.
topic.kk: Екі жұмыс мәтіні: әлеуметтік желіде жұмыс туралы не жазуға болады және жұмысқа қабылдау комиссиясы қалай жұмыс істейді.
topic.ru: Два рабочих текста: что можно писать о работе в соцсетях и как работает комиссия по найму.

items.prompt: The rules apply to what staff write on their private profiles.

explanation.en: “including posts on personal accounts” → TRUE: the rules cover private profiles too.
explanation.kk: «including posts on personal accounts» → TRUE: ереже жеке парақшаларға да қатысты.
explanation.ru: «including posts on personal accounts» → TRUE: правила касаются и личных страниц.

items.quote: Staff must not reply to customer complaints that appear online, however unfair they seem
items.prompt: Staff may answer an online complaint if they believe it is unfair.

explanation.en: “must not reply… however unfair they seem” → FALSE: not even an unfair complaint may be answered.
explanation.kk: «must not reply… however unfair they seem» → FALSE: әділетсіз шағымға да жауап беруге болмайды.
explanation.ru: «must not reply… however unfair they seem» → FALSE: отвечать нельзя даже на несправедливую жалобу.

items.quote: who aim to respond within one working day
items.prompt: Most online complaints are answered on the day they are posted.

explanation.en: “aim to respond within one working day” is only a target; how many are answered the same day is not stated → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: «aim to respond within one working day» — бөлімнің мақсаты ғана; сол күні қаншалықты жиі жауап беретіні айтылмаған → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: «aim to respond within one working day» — это цель отдела; как часто отвечают в тот же день, не сказано → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: Photographs taken at the warehouse or in the production areas must not be posted at all
items.prompt: Photographs of the warehouse may be shared if no colleagues appear in them.

explanation.en: “must not be posted at all” → FALSE: warehouse photos are banned entirely. Asking colleagues applies to other pictures.
explanation.kk: «must not be posted at all» → FALSE: қойма суретін мүлде жариялауға болмайды. Әріптестің рұқсаты — басқа суреттерге арналған ереже.
explanation.ru: «must not be posted at all» → FALSE: снимки склада нельзя публиковать вообще. Разрешение коллег — правило для других фото.

items.quote: Posts that break this guidance may be treated as a disciplinary matter.
items.prompt: Staff who break the guidance will be dismissed.

explanation.en: “may be treated as a disciplinary matter” — dismissal is never mentioned → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: «may be treated as a disciplinary matter» — тәртіптік қарау болуы мүмкін; жұмыстан шығару туралы айтылмаған → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: «may be treated as a disciplinary matter» — возможно дисциплинарное разбирательство; об увольнении ничего не сказано → NOT GIVEN.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Text A? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

items.quote: never post images that show computer screens, whiteboards or documents
items.prompt: Apart from whiteboards and documents, what must never be visible in photos taken at work?

explanation.en: “never post images that show computer screens, whiteboards or documents” → computer screens.
explanation.kk: «never post images that show computer screens, whiteboards or documents» → computer screens: қалған екеуі сұрақта аталған.
explanation.ru: «never post images that show computer screens, whiteboards or documents» → computer screens.

items.quote: should report it to their manager rather than responding to it themselves
items.prompt: Who should staff tell if they see false claims about the company online?

explanation.en: “should report it to their manager” → their manager. “The chair” comes from Text B, about knowing a candidate.
explanation.kk: «should report it to their manager» → their manager. «The chair» — Text B-дан, ол жерде таныс үміткер туралы айтылады.
explanation.ru: «should report it to their manager» → their manager. «The chair» — из Text B, там речь о знакомом кандидате.

groups.instruction: Answer the questions below about Text A. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the text for each answer.

items.prompt: Training before a first panel: roughly 8 ____ minutes online

explanation.en: “which takes about ninety minutes” → ninety. “Three years” is how often it is repeated.
explanation.kk: «which takes about ninety minutes» → ninety. «Three years» — курсты қайталау мерзімі.
explanation.ru: «which takes about ninety minutes» → ninety. «Three years» — как часто курс повторяют.

items.quote: must be repeated every three years
items.prompt: The training has to be done again every 9 ____

explanation.en: “must be repeated every three years” → three years. “Done again” = “repeated”.
explanation.kk: «must be repeated every three years» → three years. «Done again» мен «repeated» — бір мағына.
explanation.ru: «must be repeated every three years» → three years. «Done again» = «repeated».

items.quote: Panel members receive the application forms at least two working days before the interviews
items.prompt: Paperwork reaches the panel no later than 10 ____ ahead

explanation.en: “at least two working days before the interviews” → two working days. “Three working days” is when the winner is phoned.
explanation.kk: «at least two working days before the interviews» → two working days. «Three working days» — жеңімпазға қоңырау шалатын мерзім.
explanation.ru: «at least two working days before the interviews» → two working days. «Three working days» — когда звонят победителю.

items.quote: give each answer a score from one to five immediately afterwards
items.prompt: Each answer is marked on a scale from one to 11 ____

explanation.en: “give each answer a score from one to five” → five. “Marked on a scale” = “score”.
explanation.kk: «give each answer a score from one to five» → five. «Marked on a scale» мен «score» — бір мағына.
explanation.ru: «give each answer a score from one to five» → five. «Marked on a scale» = «score».

groups.title: Interview panels — the rules
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below about Text B. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the text for each answer.

items.quote: so that decisions about who to interview are based only on skills and experience
items.prompt: Why are some personal details removed before the forms are sent out?

options.text: To keep candidates’ addresses away from other candidates
So that the choice of who to interview rests on skills and experience
Because the chair makes the final decision
To reduce the time panel members spend reading

explanation.en: “so that decisions about who to interview are based only on skills and experience” → B.
explanation.kk: «so that decisions about who to interview are based only on skills and experience» → B: кімді шақыру тек білік пен тәжірибеге қарап шешіледі.
explanation.ru: «so that decisions about who to interview are based only on skills and experience» → B.

items.quote: Anyone who knows a candidate personally should tell the chair before the interviews
items.prompt: What should a panel member do if they know one of the candidates?

options.text: Tell the chair before the interviews.
Give that candidate a lower score.
Let the candidate know the result informally.

explanation.en: “should tell the chair before the interviews” → B. “Report it to their manager” is the social-media rule in Text A.
explanation.kk: «should tell the chair before the interviews» → B. «Report it to their manager» — Text A-дағы әлеуметтік желі ережесі.
explanation.ru: «should tell the chair before the interviews» → B. «Report it to their manager» — правило из Text A про соцсети.
